boundary: This establishes a bounded exact execution-hexis law over source-faced typed DAGs whose operations are supplied by the application world. It does not claim that arbitrary inscriptions reveal their own latent operations without returned paths, nor that ADD and CONCAT exhaust path species. The open construction is plural and nested DAG cultivation across further exact world operations, not a vocabulary or answer table.
conclusion: After the six declared teacher paths departed, the remounted ecology received unseen 1+4. Under the arithmetic receiver it rebuilt Literal(1), Literal(4), Add(0,1), Return(2) and returned exact integer 5. Under the concatenate receiver it rebuilt the same causal shape with text literals and returned 14. With objective withheld it retained both. On 1+2+3 the two valid slot placements remained two distinct paths even though their returned text coincided. Thus the learned object is the receiver-relative transport law joining a surface to a complete executable path, not a stored strongest edge or a scalar answer.
question: Can recurrent complete execution paths become a receiver-relative exact ecology that re-instantiates an unseen path after every teacher path has departed?
stopping_condition: Stop when one source-absent remount re-instantiates the complete ADD path for unseen 1+4 and returns exact 5, the same surface under CONCAT returns text 14, withholding objective preserves both, ambiguous slot placement stays plural, an unafforded surface returns no path, all teacher and replaced carriers depart, and the complete ecology survives exact rest.
theory_to_structure: The inscription fold supplies addressable constituent incidence; the returned typed DAG supplies the transported operation. Ordered literal faces divide each inscription into exact constant segments and open slots. Recurrence makes that surface/path relation addressable. A later receiver binds new exact faces, re-instantiates the entire DAG, and only then obtains its consequence. Objective is one local receiver axis: it selects ADD or CONCAT for the same glyph surface, while its absence preserves both.
